core_obligations: One direction (proof lines 12291-12302): the pullback of a constructible sheaf along any morphism is constructible, since the preimage of a partition into locally closed constructible strata is again such a partition in the quasi-compact quasi-separated case.

Converse (proof lines 12302-12314): for a surjective f and a sheaf whose pullback is constructible, the author deduces that the sheaf itself is constructible by transporting the partition of X to Y along the surjection, which is legitimate because f is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
Conclude for the three settings (proof lines 12314-12318): the arguments for sheaves of sets, abelian sheaves and sheaves of modules over a Noetherian ring are the same in each case.
proof_roadmap: Show that pullback preserves constructibility, which is the easy direction.
For the converse, transport a partition of X along the surjection f to obtain one for Y.
Apply the same argument in the three settings of the statement.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that constructibility of a sheaf on a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme can be tested after a surjective morphism of such schemes, in the three settings of sheaves of sets, abelian sheaves and modules over a Noetherian ring (statement lines 12275-12289). One direction is the stability of constructibility under pullback (proof lines 12291-12302); the converse requires transporting a partition of the source along the surjection, using the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness hypotheses (proof lines 12302-12314), after which the three settings are treated uniformly (proof lines 12314-12318). The non-formal content is the transport of the partition along the surjection. The claim is H2: one easy direction plus one transport argument.
